title: Allisha Gray injury: Dream star 'making progress,' status for WNBA Finals unclear - CBS Sports
description: Gray was declared available about 30 minutes before tip-off after missing most of the semis with a hand injury
body:
Gray was declared available about 30 minutes before tip-off after missing most of the semis with a hand injury
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:08 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        OAKLAND, Calif. -- Dream guard Allisha Gray will be available to play in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries, the team announced just 30 minutes before tip-off. Gray injured her finger during Game 1 of the semifinals against the New York Liberty and sat out the rest of the series, which the Dream swept in three games. "I felt good, the shot felt good, dribble felt good, hand felt good," Gray told reporters after her warm-up on Saturday, when she was still waiting to be cleared by medical staff. "Either I'm a full go and 100%, or if I'm not, I'm not going to go out there thinking about this hand, because it doesn't help my team."
Gray, whose 19 points per game led the Dream in scoring and ranked ninth in the league, talked about her recovery after the Dream practiced on Friday."My hand feels good. Today in practice was really my first day of actually being able to have a full practice, go through contact and stuff like that," Gray said. "Right now I'm still day-to-day and then we're gonna see how my finger reacts to how practice went today and we'll see tomorrow."
Gray, who still had the pinky and ring fingers on her left shooting hand taped together, said she doesn't think about her finger when she's on the court, and was "just so happy" to be able to "run up and down the court and be able to shoot." 
Gray recently underwent a "minor" procedure on her left hand after she injured it during Game 1 of the semifinals against the New York Liberty. Specifics regarding her injury and the timing and extent of the procedure remain unclear. Early in that contest in Brooklyn, she deflected a pass from Sabrina Ionescu. After a short trip to the locker room, Gray returned to the game with tape on her fingers. Her first shot was a bad miss from 3-point range, so she removed the tape. In the second quarter, she made another nice defensive play on Ionescu, but aggravated the injury in the process and has not played since. 
Dream's title chances may hinge on Gray's availability"Allisha's one of the best players in the W," Dream coach Karl Smesko said Tuesday. "To advance and beat a great New York team basically without her, except for 10 minutes of one game, is a testament to everybody else raising their game. But it would be great to have her back for the Finals. She's just somebody that, offensively, is really hard to stop, and then she makes defensive plays. She's just an all-around great player."
        
            
                2026 WNBA playoffs bracket: WNBA Finals schedule tweaked so Dream can use larger venue
                
                    Lindsay Gibbs                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The Dream's ability to beat the Valkyries and win the first championship in franchise history may hinge on Gray's availability. Jordin Canada, DeWanna Bonner and Isobel Borlase were spectacular in the semifinals against the Liberty, but it's a big ask for them to repeat these performances:Canada had three of the five-highest playoff scoring performances of her career against the Liberty, and averaged 22.3 points on 62.2/61.5/100 shooting splits -- up from 11.6 points on 43.1/29.2/78.2 shooting in the regular season. Bonner went for 15.3 points and 8.3 rebounds on 50/46.7/80 shooting splits, up from 10.4 points and six rebounds on 40.2/27.9/84.3 shooting between the Phoenix Mercury and Dream in the regular season. And Borlase, who only had six double-digit scoring games in the regular season, came off the bench to chip in 11 points in Game 2 and 10 points in Game 3 while shooting 9 of 15, including 3 of 6 from 3-point range. The Valkyries have the best defense in the league by a wide margin, and just shut down A'ja Wilson and Jackie Young in a sweep of the Las Vegas Aces. Even acknowledging the Valkyries' own issues on offense, it's hard to imagine how the Dream would be able to score enough points to beat them without Gray. 
While Gray will clearly not be 100% if she suits up, having an All-WNBA-caliber talent on the floor that the Valkyries have to respect would make life far easier for the Dream.

schema.headline: Allisha Gray injury: Dream star 'making progress,' status for WNBA Finals unclear - CBS Sports

title: The Spurs will start Dylan Harper on opening night, so where does that leave De'Aaron Fox? - CBS Sports
description: The Spurs will try out a three-guard lineup again at the start of this season with Harper, Fox and Stephon Castle
body:
The Spurs will try out a three-guard lineup again at the start of this season with Harper, Fox and Stephon Castle
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:05 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        For opening night, at least, the San Antonio Spurs have answered the single biggest starting lineup question of the 2026-27 season. Dylan Harper, the No. 2 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft and the second-best player in San Antonio's NBA Finals loss to the New York Knicks, will officially join the starting five alongside Victor Wembanyama, Stephon Castle, Devin Vassell... and De'Aaron Fox, the expensive veteran whose injured ankle and ensuing struggles loomed large over that Finals defeat.San Antonio barely used the three-guard lineup last season, and for good reason. It was outscored significantly in both 54-possession regular-season and 83-possession postseason samples last year. The lineup outscored the Phoenix Suns by 10 points in 25 possessions in a recent preseason victory, but the Spurs shot just 2 of 9 on 3s when all three guards played together in that game.That is the primary concern here. Harper, Fox and Castle are all strong drivers with questionable 3-point shots. Such players typically do best when surrounded by other shooters. The Spurs can get away with having two of them on the floor at once because their center, Victor Wembanyama, is game-breaking in dozens of ways, including his ability to space the floor. San Antonio took off last season when it upgraded its shooting by inserting Julian Champagnie into the starting lineup.With all three guards playing together, though, the delicate balance between shooting and ball-handling has tilted too far toward the latter. Ball-handling doesn't have nearly the amplifying effect that shooting does, and opponents will inevitably cheat off of the two guards without the ball in their hands whenever one of them is trying to create shots with it. The trio is so talented, and comes with the inherent advantage of playing with Wembanyama, that the Spurs will almost certainly win most of the games it plays with this starting lineup. 

        
            
                Ranking the NBA's top 100 players: Victor Wembanyama enters 2026-27 season at No. 1
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
But it's certainly suboptimal. We all know where this is probably heading. Harper was simply too good to keep coming off of the bench, and Castle is too good to ever move there. Eventually, the best version of the Spurs likely has Fox, the oldest and most expensive of the three guards, coming off of the bench as Harper did a season ago. San Antonio's starters with Champagnie playing alongside two of the guards outscored opponents by 17.6 points per 100 possessions a season ago. The formula of two guards, two shooters and Wembanyama is this team's endgame.Yet even if that's the case, the Spurs are slow-playing this. In the long run, that's probably the sensible approach. Benching a reigning All-Star on a max contract is fraught. Fox very intentionally steered himself to San Antonio through a direct trade request, presumably expecting to be the starting point guard on a dynasty. Players of his stature and age are rarely eager to come off of the bench. Asking him to do so on opening night based off of a poor Finals series in which he was injured risks alienating a key player and, cynically, destroying what little trade value he might have left.Even if the Spurs do plan to bench Fox down the line, easing him into it seems like the safest approach. He still has a chance to prove that this three-guard lineup can work, and if it does, well, maybe there's less of a problem here than we're assuming. If it proves uncomfortable or if the lineup data suggests it's flopping, the Spurs at least have empirical data supporting a change. They can at least tell Fox that they tried.
They'd hardly be the first team to try this approach to benching a star. Russell Westbrook went through it with both Los Angeles teams, for instance. The Lakers benched him after an 0-3 start in the 2022-23 season. The Clippers let him and James Harden start five games together a year later, lost all five, and then went 27-7 in their next 34 after benching him. Sometimes, you have to sacrifice a few games for the greater good. Players of this caliber tend to expect a certain degree of respect that the attempt at least affords.The notion of sacrificing games is going to be a bitter pill to swallow in this case, specifically, because San Antonio's competition for the No. 1 seed in the Western Conference practically never does so. The Oklahoma City Thunder churn out 60-win seasons in their sleep, and home-court advantage in the practically preordained Western Conference Finals between them, despite San Antonio's road victory a year ago, is meaningful. But that same road victory showed the Spurs that what matters isn't October or November. It's May and June. If the Spurs have to take the long road to optimized lineups and locker room harmony, so be it. For now, they're giving Harper the starting job he so clearly deserves and tabling the Fox end of the equation until the issue is forced.

title: UFC Fight Night predictions, fight card, odds for Joaquin Buckley vs. Mike Malott - CBS Sports
description: The pair of veteran welterweights collide in a pivotal fight on Canadian soil
body:
The pair of veteran welterweights collide in a pivotal fight on Canadian soil
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:20 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Captain Canada comes home with his self-anointed "Maple Leaf Militia." Mike Malott makes his seventh straight start in Canada on Saturday, headlining in his home nation in back-to-back fights. This time, he wants Joaquin Buckley's No. 10 welterweight ranking at UFC Fight Night in Edmonton.This is make-or-break for Buckley (21-8). "New Mansa," a reference to the historical Mali Empire ruler Mansa Musa, seemed to be on his own conquest after he knocked out former title challengers Stephen Thompson and Colby Covington. Buckley has always shown potential; look no further than his iconic spinning back kick KO against Impa Kasanganay. Unfortunately, dominant grappling losses to Kamaru Usman and Sean Brady completely halted his momentum. His confidence remains intact, even if outside belief is dwindling, as he defends his spot in the welterweight Top 10 this weekend."I thought I was very, very, very prepared for Sean Brady. I thought I was, to be honest, and Sean Brady came in and did his job," Buckley told CBS Sports. "But I can't be concerned about what the other man is going to do. I just have to put myself in a position where I'm always on the offensive. And a great offense is a great defense."Malott (14-2-1) has a very unique role in the UFC ecosystem. He's essentially become the North Star for a Great White North sorely in need of it. It's been nearly four years since Malott has fought outside of Canada. His first main event, which took place in April, saw him knock out and retire longtime contender Gilbert Burns. If Malott can stop Buckley, who is two years younger than him despite being the UFC veteran, he'll be on a collision course with the division's top names.
"There are definitely things we saw in studying him that we believe we can take advantage of in all aspects of fighting," Malott told CBS Sports. "I don't love scripting a fight. I'm more focused on preparation than prediction... Man, fighting is chaos. Preparing the skills for whatever could arise, going in there and jamming, feeling it out, and taking where I feel right. I've done that pretty much every time, and it's worked well for me." 
The co-main event has even more immediate title implications than the main event. The women's flyweight division is radically changing after Valentina Shevchenko vacated her title earlier this year due to injury. Natalia Silva defeated Wang Cong to become the new champion at UFC 332. That ticks off Erin Blanchfield. Long, labeled a future title challenger, Blanchfield believes she deserved the opportunity that ultimately went to Cong. A statement win against Jasmine Jasudavicius is paramount this weekend, especially with Alexa Grasso's resurgence and Shevchenko's inevitable return."They didn't reach out to me. My manager and I reached out to them because I wanted to put my hat in, if that was an option or opportunity," Blanchfield said. "They wanted Wang Cong to take that fight, and I had my fight already. That definitely sucked a bit in the moment, but I had to quickly say, 'Whatever, that's not happening.' I have this fight. I need to perform, and everything else can come after that."
Let's take a look at the rest of the fight card with the latest odds from DraftKings before getting to a prediction and expert pick on the main event below.UFC Fight Night card, oddsFavoriteUnderdogWeightclassMike Malott -135Joaquin Buckley +114WelterweightErin Blanchfield -325Jasmine Jasudavicius +260Women's flyweightCristian Perez -340Kyle Nelson +270LightweightKyle Daukaus -185Marc-Andre Barriault +154MiddleweightLouis Jourdain -180Timmy Cuamba +150BantamweightMandel Nallo -285  Nate Landwehr +230  LightweightUFC Fight Night viewing informationDate: Saturday, Oct. 17 | Start time: 8 p.m. ET (Main card), 5 p.m. (Prelims)Location: Rogers Place -- Edmonton, CanadaTV Channel: Paramount+ (subscribe now for as low as $8.99 per month)          PredictionJoaquin Buckley vs. Mike Malott: There are serious questions about Buckley's defensive grappling. That cannot be denied. But I'm not sure Malott, despite his grappling trophies, can capitalize as Usman and Brady did. Buckley showed great wrestling defense against Colby Covington and has been competing in Real American Freestyle. He hasn't had a good run there, but he's diligently patching that hole. It's more complicated on the feet. I believe Malott, the former striking coach at Team Alpha Male, is the better technical striker even though he lacks Buckley's flashiness. Malott will have early success, but it's the late game that worries me. Malott's loss to Neil Magny taught him to pace himself. How that translates to five rounds, however, is still a mystery. By contrast, we've seen Buckley winging punches at Usman in the fifth round of an exhausting fight. Buckley could start taking over partway through Round 3, if the fight lasts that long. Buckley's chin is far from foolproof, but his defensive sensibilities have improved drastically over the years. If this fight goes long, which I'm predicting it will, Buckley should sneak ahead and even stop an exhausted Malott. Pick: Buckley via KO, Round 4.

title: How the Washington Spirit found their playoff form in a gritty 1-0 win over NWSL rivals Gotham FC - CBS Sports
description: Lucia Di Guglielmo's first league goal secured a 1-0 victory over first-place Gotham FC at Audi Field, halting th
body:
Lucia Di Guglielmo's first league goal secured a 1-0 victory over first-place Gotham FC at Audi Field, halting the reigning champions from locking up the regular-season crown
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:39 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Washington Spirit punched their ticket to the 2026 NWSL playoffs, and the NWSL Shield just got more interesting. The Spirit defeated Gotham FC, the reigning NWSL Championship winners, 1-0, at Audi Field on Saturday.The two teams gave audiences a glimpse of playoff-caliber action, with high stakes. Gotham FC leads the league table with 55 points but has not yet clinched the NWSL Shield, and the loss means they'll have to try again next weekend. The win keeps Washington Spirit in contention for the NWSL Shield and marks the club's third consecutive postseason return since Michelle Kang's takeover in 2022. Newly acquired Lucia Di Guglielmo scored the decisive goal; it's the Italian international's first NWSL goal and the Spirit's first against Gotham since November 2024, during the 2024 NWSL semifinals.Spirit spoil Gotham's shield partyThe win carries big implications, and the way the Spirit spoiled Gotham's form and clinched a playoff spot says even more. The scene setter for the Spirit wasn't hard to miss, as Audi Field is often referred to as "rowdy," and consistent effort earns cheers as loud as goals.
Gotham's injury woes appeared to catch up to them with rookie Jordynn Dudley out for the season with a foot fracture, and Jaedyn Shaw as an unused sub. Shaw left USWNT U23 camps early as a precaution following an injury, and was not listed as unavailable for Saturday's match, but was not utilized after warming up at various points of the match. But ultimately, the reigning champions have a deep bench and couldn't generate more offense despite having more of the ball. Even with a deliberate game plan by Spirit head coach Adrian Gonzalez to absorb more and have less of the ball by design, the Spirit created more shots (13) and more shots on target (six) than Gotham despite losing the possession battle. 
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            "Today [it] was key to be very compact, narrow, protecting the middle a lot. And then I think we've done a good job with Esme [Morgan] with T [Rudd] stepping, jumping to those pockets, and not allowing them to receive comfortably there," Gonzalez said after the game.
"Overall, the team I think has done a great job at different heights. I think, pressing high, forcing them to play long. Anytime that they wanted to play back, I think we've stepped really good, making their attack more uncomfortable. And in a mid-low block situation, I think the team has defended pretty good."Spirit midfield is healingFrom newly acquired players to long-time members of the Spirit, it felt like a turning of the page for the Spirit into a mode of the season they aren't unfamiliar with; the playoff grind.Tanzania international Clara Luvanga wasn't on the score sheet but was a constant mark for Gotham in the final third, with her hold-up play, distributing the ball wide, and being a threat on goal in the first half. Team captain and Spirit veteran Andi Sullivan is back from maternity leave, getting starting minutes again, and the return of Leicy Santos, even on a minutes restriction, reminded everyone why she was such a missed piece of the equation while on the injury list. 
"Obviously we've missed her, all of us. It's been a process, and we've tried to be very cautious and prudent, especially not to push her too hard, because she's accumulated a lot of minutes with us and with the national team. It was especially important for her to reach this final stretch in optimal condition so she could help us, without making the mistake of trying to bring her back too quickly," Gonzalez said."She was ready to play 45 minutes today, and I think she gave the team a lot. Once again, she showed her talent. Even after being out for a long time, she has the ability to make an impact in a game like this. In 45 minutes, she showed her quality on the ball, her ability to find the final pass, and her personality in competing and defending. She brings us a great deal. Going forward, we'll continue to be cautious, make sure her progress is right, and gradually see how she settles back in. We'll try to add minutes little by little, knowing that we still have several matches ahead."Santo's minutes restriction opened the door for Melissa Bethi to have her own impact on the game. The Algerian international was acquired midseason and joined the team following the Women's African Cup of Nations and delivered the game-winning assist to Di Guglielmo.
"I mean, it's like a dream, or even more, because it's kind of the perfect situation, the perfect first goal, perfect win, and everything is special here," Di Guglielmo said after the game.NWSL Shield race heats upWhile Saturday's win clinched another playoff appearance for the Spirit, it also keeps them in the mix for the NWSL Shield. It's one of the more interesting races in league history, as three teams, including the San Diego Wave, are in the hunt with just a few games remaining. The Spirit aren't getting ahead of themselves, though, as Sullivan knows anything can happen and there's always work to be done.  "I'm still focused on this next regular season game; I think that's the attitude we need to have. I think there can be a lot of like narratives about the past two seasons and playoffs and everything, but the most important thing is the week in front of you and putting yourself and your team in the best situation to win the game in front of you ... because you know you can't get too far ahead of yourself too early," Sullivan said.  "That's kind of the messaging that I'll be spreading to the team, and I think that's something that we can always improve on is focusing on the task at hand."

title: Ohio State survived Indiana, but Julian Sayin's injury may decide season - CBS Sports
description: With the Buckeyes' star quarterback out "several weeks," and challenging Big Ten opponents on deck, the trajector
body:
With the Buckeyes' star quarterback out "several weeks," and challenging Big Ten opponents on deck, the trajectory of Ohio State's season is very much up in the air
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:47 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        College football can be a brutal sport. Sometimes victory can be taken from you by a toe or two; other times, it comes at a serious cost. That was the case Saturday in Ohio State's 19-15 win over Indiana, a game neither team escaped feeling whole.Indiana's 22-game win streak came to an end in an extremely painful manner. Down five late, on a fourth-and-4 at the Ohio State 27, Indiana opted to go for the throat instead of the first down. Josh Hoover dropped back, found a wide-open Nick Marsh down the sideline, and hit him in stride.
But that stride was debilitating. Marsh's left foot came down out of bounds, and he knew it immediately. The look on his face was heartbreaking.That misery wasn't felt on the Ohio State sideline. Instead, it was relief, but with questions about what's to come. The primary reason Indiana had a chance to win the game late was that Ohio State's starting QB Julian Sayin was knocked out of the game with an apparent right arm injury earlier in the fourth quarter. 
After taking a vicious hit from Indiana's Mario Landino, Sayin was seen running to the Ohio State locker room, right arm hanging by his side. He emerged a few minutes later with it in a sling, as the diminutive true freshman Luke Fahey filled in for him, and the Buckeyes offense ground to a complete halt.The Buckeyes didn't manage a first down with Fahey in the game, so while they survived the trip to Bloomington, got revenge on the Hoosiers for last season's Big Ten Championship, and avoided a perilous second loss, there are suddenly concerning questions lingering around the program.Ohio State coach Ryan Day said after the game, without going into specifics about the injury, that Sayin would be out "several weeks."

        
            
                Ohio State QB Julian Sayin to miss 'several weeks' after suffering injury in win vs. Indiana
                
                    Robby Kalland                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The good news is Ohio State is off next week. The bad news is that when the Buckeyes return from their respite, they'll be on the road to face USC, and then it's a home game with Oregon. While both those teams have had their issues in 2026, the prospect of having to face both with a true freshman at QB is not one that should excite anybody in Scarlet and Gray.If Sayin is out even longer, there are games left against a Northwestern team that's now 5-1 after beating Michigan State, as well as a road game against the Nebraska team that gave Indiana fits last week. Oh, and there's Michigan too.While Buckeyes fans everywhere celebrate this win, they'll do so while awaiting an injury report that could determine the fate of their season.

schema.headline: Ohio State survived Indiana, but Julian Sayin's injury may decide season - CBS Sports

title: Florida stuns No. 7 Texas in Austin, handing tumbling Longhorns second-consecutive loss - CBS Sports
description: After climbing to No. 1 early in the season, the Longhorns are on the ropes after back-to-back losses
body:
After climbing to No. 1 early in the season, the Longhorns are on the ropes after back-to-back losses
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:45 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Trailing 17-3 to Texas in the second quarter in Austin, the Florida Gators looked like they were headed for a third consecutive loss after their red-hot start to the Jon Sumrall era. Sophomore quarterback Tramell Jones was struggling in his first career start in hostile territory, and in spite of a lackluster effort from Arch Manning, the Longhorns seemed like they were going to roll to a needed bounce back victory after the disaster in Red River. A late second quarter touchdown provided a bit of life and confidence for Jones and the Gators, and Florida quickly tied things up on their first drive of the second half to raise the anxiety level in Darrell K. Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Suddenly, the Texas offense couldn't move the ball and the Gators offense had found life, with star running back Jadan Baugh shaking off a few rough weeks to help take the pressure off his young quarterback with some key runs in the fourth quarter. 
The Gators ripped off 24 unanswered points on Texas to take a 10-point lead in the fourth quarter on a Baugh touchdown run with just over six minutes to play. 
As he did against Ohio State earlier this year, Arch Manning found his best once again while trailing in the fourth quarter at home. Manning produced an unreal throw on fourth-and-7 to keep the Longhorns hopes alive and then delivered a strike for a touchdown to cut the deficit to three. After forcing a three-and-out, Texas seemed like it had seized all the momentum before disaster struck in the form of an Arch Manning fumble as he got sacked, handing the Gators the ball with a chance to run out the clock. 
Jones would put the game on ice with a nifty third down run to get a first down after Texas had burned all of its timeouts, and the Gators got into victory formation for a huge 27-24 win on the road. 
What the loss means for TexasThe Longhorns make some unfortunate history by blowing another first-half lead, as 2026 Texas is the first AP No. 1 to lose back-to-back games to unranked opponents since 1961. For Steve Sarkisian, it's another disappointing season with lofty expectations, and even with a massive contract, things are going to start warming up for Sark in Austin. While Texas has undoubtedly raised its floor in the Sarkisian era, the expectation for Texas, given its investment in the program, is to compete for national championships. That's yet to happen, and at 4-2 the Longhorns now have an extremely small margin for error in the second half of the season if they want to make the College Football Playoff. Adding to the Longhorns' problems going forward is the uncertain status of star pass rusher Colin Simmons, who went down with an apparent leg injury in the fourth quarter and did not return after leaving for the locker room on a cart. Simmons' 10.5 sacks on the season lead the nation, and in his absence, the Texas defense lacks the same ability to pressure the quarterback. 
Given the defense has been carrying the load much of the season, that shifts more pressure to Arch Manning and the offense to figure things out. Saturday was once again a Jekyll and Hyde performance from Manning, as he produced a handful of incredible throws but also made some disastrous mistakes -- most notably the game-sealing fumble while being sacked. Heading into Week 8, seemingly everything is on the table in Austin, as the Longhorns have gone from the top of the college football world to desperation mode in record time. What the win means for FloridaAll the excitement from the hot start for Jon Sumrall's Gators had been stripped away by back-to-back rough losses, dropping Florida out of the polls. With Aaron Philo injured, it seemed like things had gone from bad to worse, but now the Gators are right back in the mix at 5-2 and will be thinking about a second-half run in the SEC. 
While it would take an undefeated run from here to likely make the College Football Playoff, Sumrall now seems to be locked in to having his first season in Gainesville viewed as a major success. Florida's defense ranked as the worst in the SEC coming into this game, but they produced some huge plays to force a couple of turnovers to help out their young quarterback. That young QB also gives the Gators some confidence going forward that they can compete whether it's Jones or Philo under center -- and if anything, there's a question of whether Florida is better off with the dynamic sophomore running the show, given what he showed in Austin with his arm and legs.

schema.headline: Florida stuns No. 7 Texas in Austin, handing tumbling Longhorns second-consecutive loss - CBS Sports

title: How good can Barcelona be? Eleven wins straight and counting to start the season - CBS Sports
description: With 39 goals in nine league games and Lamine Yamal ascending to another level, Hansi Flick's squad has built an
body:
With 39 goals in nine league games and Lamine Yamal ascending to another level, Hansi Flick's squad has built an unstoppable juggernaut
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:46 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It's 11 matches, 11 wins as Hansi Flick's Barcelona continue their perfect start to the season by defeating Real Betis 5-2. Who else but Lamine Yamal opened the scoring? In his age-19 season, he's taking a step forward despite already being a global superstar, which is scary for the rest of the world.  Flick's men have dispatched every team in their path, and even that level of dominance doesn't do justice to what Barcelona have done this season. Barcelona executed their summer transfers to perfection, and while it's too early to begin discussing a perfect season, it's clear that they have the best attack in the world, and it isn't particularly close. Raphinha missed their last three matches due to injury, and the club didn't miss his 14 goals in all competitions, winning each match by three goals.  It was slightly tougher facing Manuel Pellegrini's Real Betis, but if a team has to score four goals to have a chance of beating Barcelona this season, it brings an immense amount of pressure. Betis are off to an excellent start to the season with six wins in nine LaLiga matches, but they've scored 23 fewer goals than Barcelona. Yes, you read that correctly: 23 fewer goals. In fact, no LaLiga team has come within 20 goals of matching Barcelona's 39 goals in nine games.
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            While they've gotten off to an impressive start to the season, it's also worth looking at how they've done it.Hitting the mark on transfersOver the summer, Barcelona added Anthony Gordon, Karim Adeyemi, Gabriel Jesus and Rodri as they've finally gotten to a point where they can spend money again. Not only have the new attackers added speed in transition, but Rodri has also marshaled the defense so the squad is caught out in transition less often. Those new signings have also accounted for seven LaLiga goals between them and have also given Flick serious depth to rotate while also competing on multiple fronts.  While it's true Barcelona are still conceding goals with Rodri in midfield due to their open play style, only five teams have conceded fewer goals than Barcelona, they don't need to have a stout defense, just one that's good enough to let their historic attack go to work. Keeping things in line is what will help this team contend for a Champions League crown, which is still the goal. Yamal keeps goingWeirdly, last season was a down season for Lamine Yamal as he missed time with injuries and was "only" involved in 27 LaLiga goals. Now he has scored eight and assisted six more in only nine games played as he's reaching yet another level. There are too many superlatives to describe what he's doing on the pitch, but his dribbling, vision and finishing are off the charts. 

                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            In Champions League play, he took a Galatasaray defender for a ride along the sideline before setting up Anthony Gordon for a goal, and with how much talent is around him, Barcelona can maximize what Yamal does well. 
Yamal is already a Ballon d'Or contender, and the fact that he's still improving his game means the rest of the world will need to look out. He's already doing things that haven't been done by anyone who isn't named Lionel Messi, and we're only scratching the surface of this potential. Sometimes players who break out at such a young age can plateau and stay at the same level for years, but when you're seeing clear improvement from him in a juggernaut of a team, anything could happen here. Even a perfect season -- it's too early to talk about one yet, but it could happen.
Strikers on strikersEven though he hasn't played in three games, it wouldn't be right to talk about Barcelona without mentioning the exploits of Raphinha and his position change. Flick has pushed him centrally to be a striker, and it has worked to perfection. He's leading the European Golden Shoe rankings for the top scorer across Europe's leagues, and you'd think that he has been a striker for his entire career. It's impressive management from Flick, and with Gabriel Jesus as the backup, the squad isn't missing a step even without their star man in the middle. It helps keep up the attacking pressure, and with a Clasico against Real Madrid looming next week, Barcelona can turn all of this into a commanding lead in LaLiga.

schema.headline: How good can Barcelona be? Eleven wins straight and counting to start the season - CBS Sports

title: Eagles to place Jalen Hurts on IR, as he deals with superficial blood clot, per report - CBS Sports
description: Hurts is out indefinitely and will miss the game against the Panthers on Sunday, and at least three more
body:
Hurts is out indefinitely and will miss the game against the Panthers on Sunday, and at least three more
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:05 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Philadelphia Eagles are placing quarterback Jalen Hurts, who is out this week with a superficial blood clot, on injured reserve, the team officially announced on Saturday, after consultations with numerous doctors and experts. Going on IR sidelines a player for at least four weeks, meaning Hurts will miss this weekend's game, as the team previously announced, along with three divisional games.He will miss matchups against the Carolina Panthers, Dallas Cowboys, Washington Commanders and New York Giants. Hurts will be eligible to return against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Nov. 22, but that doesn't mean he is guaranteed to be back then. With Hurts out, Tanner McKee will be leading the offense, and rookie Cole Payton will be the backup. The Eagles released a statement saying Hurts requested treatment on his calf four days after their Week 4 loss against the Los Angeles Rams. The Eagles performed an ultrasound on his leg after they landed in London for their game against the Jacksonville Jaguars and found the superficial blood clot. The team's medical staff determined he could play, and the team conducted a follow-up ultrasound where they found the blood clot had moved, which can lead to a serious health situation. 
When he can play will be determined by his medical team, meaning he could miss more than just four games. Hurts is still working on the best treatment plan for the situation and the team believes it is treatable. Hurts and the team are both still looking into more options and are putting the quarterback's health as top priority. 
        
            
                Jalen Hurts blood clot: Expert weighs in on Eagles' situation, and when QB could return to the field
                
                    Jordan Dajani                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Blood thinners are a main treatment for blood clots and a player cannot play while on that medication. Typically, a patient would be on blood thinners for six weeks, but if the clot is minor, it may be treatable with other measures, such as anti-inflammatories. If the clot worsens, it could mean more time on blood thinners, which would, in turn, mean more time away from the field. 
The Eagles added some security in the quarterback position this week, signing Joe Milton off the Dallas Cowboys practice squad.

title: Texas' CFP path grows precarious after Florida upset leaves no room for error - CBS Sports
description: Where the Longhorns go from here, and how Florida can climb back into the playoff race
body:
Where the Longhorns go from here, and how Florida can climb back into the playoff race
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:36 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Arch Manning struggled, Steve Sarkisian ran out of answers, and the Longhorns lost their top defensive player to injury in the second half.No. 7 Texas had an opportunity to steady its season against skidding Florida, but instead the Longhorns made their College Football Playoff math considerably uncomfortable following a 27-24 upset loss to the Gators.This feels like a critical turn in the wrong direction for Sarkisian this season, after defending his quarterback following last week's loss to Oklahoma and now must live with another disheartening result for a team that was ranked No. 1 in college football earlier this month.Texas led 17-3 in the second quarter before the Gators ran off 24 consecutive points to lead 27-17 prior to a late rally from the Longhorns. Manning's only touchdown pass, a 9-yard strike to Cam Coleman with 4:21 left, pulled Texas within three points at 27-24.
However, after the Longhorns retained possession following a Florida punt with 2:32 left, Manning was sacked and lost a fumble on second down.Entering Week 7, the Longhorns were slotted in the College Football Playoff in our bowl projections at CBS Sports under the assumption that at least one more loss was coming for Texas this season.Now? Florida has played its way back into the discussion, while the Longhorns have left themselves very little margin for error the rest of the way and may take the field without their top defensive player, Colin Simmons, moving forward.
After beating nationally ranked Ohio State and Tennessee in September, Texas has lost consecutive games to unranked teams, falling from No. 1 in the AP poll to likely outside the top 10 in Sunday's updated rankings. Over the next four games, the Longhorns play Ole Miss, Mississippi State, at Missouri and at LSU -- all teams currently ranked inside the top 25.Manning's two interceptions in the fourth quarter of last week's loss to Oklahoma cost the Longhorns, and now, a critical fumble ended his streak of 11 wins as a starter at home for Texas.The opportunity for quality wins remains for Texas, and that matters. However, banking on a turnaround requires believing this team can suddenly deliver the consistency it has struggled to find the last few weeks with a signal caller who's not playing with confidence as a passer.
Florida's path to CFPBehind quarterback Tramell Jones, who started for the injured Aaron Philo, the Gators (5-2, 3-2) head into their open date with extra time to prepare for their battle with top-ranked Georgia inside Atlanta's Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Oct. 31. A win over the Bulldogs almost certainly pushes Florida back inside the top 15 ahead of the CFP Selection Committee's first set of rankings in November.From there, Jon Sumrall's team plays Oklahoma, at Kentucky, Vanderbilt and Florida State with a clear path to 10 wins.
Sumrall said entering Saturday's game at Texas that it was vital for his team to flush their last two outings and focus on the task at hand from here -- beating the Longhorns and getting back on track this fall."We have not responded well, and there is something to that," Sumrall said. "There is a belief, a confidence, an intestinal fortitude of  'I'm going to fight till the finish, don't even care about what the scoreboard says, and then we'll look at the end of the game and see what the scoreboard says,' and so that is a concern of mine. "It is something I saw and felt the last two games that we've got to get corrected."
The Gators responded with their second win of the season over a top-10 opponent after previously crushing Ole Miss in Gainesville.

title: Steve Sarkisian buyout, contract details as Texas football coach - CBS Sports
description: A second straight loss to an unranked opponent has the temperature rising in Austin
body:
A second straight loss to an unranked opponent has the temperature rising in Austin
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:14 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Texas Longhorns made some unfortunate history on Saturday, becoming the first program since 1961 to be ranked No. 1 in the AP poll and then lose back-to-back games to unranked opponents. After blowing a lead in the Red River Rivalry against Oklahoma, Texas jumped out to another big first-half lead against Florida on Saturday before the Gators, led by backup quarterback Tramell Jones, mounted a comeback for a win in Austin that has the temperature rising under Steve Sarkisian. Sark was brought into Texas to do two things. The first was to raise the floor and make them a consistently good football team. That he's accomplished, going 35-8 in his last three seasons. The second thing he was supposed to do once he raised the floor was to turn Texas into a perennial title contender. That has yet to happen despite being ranked No. 1 in the AP poll at different points in each of the last two seasons, and the Longhorns once again appear headed towards a year outside the nation's elite tier at 4-2. There is a question of whether Sarkisian is the coach to get Texas to that final step needed to win their first national title in 20 years, but if Texas were interested in making a change, it'd cost the Longhorns boosters an awful lot of money. 
Steve Sarkisian buyout, contract details Sarkisian received a new contract in 2025 that extended his tenure through 2031 and raised his salary to one of the highest in college football. Including this season, Sarkisian's contract is for six more years and just over $70 million. His buyout calls for him to be paid 85% of his remaining contract balance, which would mean Texas would be on the hook for $50.15 million after the conclusion of the 2026 season. That wouldn't be the biggest contract buyout in history -- or even the state of Texas -- but it would still be in the top five of the biggest buyouts ever. To pay that much, it would require Texas to not just be frustrated with Sarkisian, but to be completely convinced he can't get the Longhorns to the pinnacle of the sport. Texas would also have to be certain they have a better coach lined up, and while they have the resources to tempt any coach in the country, there isn't an obvious choice for the Longhorns. 
As of now, two losses don't doom Texas from being a College Football Playoff team. Given their win over Ohio State, they could very well become the first team to make it with three losses, but if Sarkisian's Longhorns were to miss the playoff entirely, given where they were after Week 5, perhaps the chatter that exists mostly in frustration online could turn into a real exploration of their options in Austin.

The Cougars are fresh off a Big 12 title game appearance only three years after joining the power conferences. The Fighting Irish and Cougars have played seven times in history, with Notre Dame holding a 5-2 advantage. No running back cleared 21 yards on the ground, bringing up the significant question of how the Cougars can generate offense against the elite Notre Dame defensive front.

title: Bears expected to start Caleb Williams vs. Falcons, per report - CBS Sports
description: The Chicago Bears are likely getting their No. 1 pick back this week
body:
The Chicago Bears are likely getting their No. 1 pick back this week
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:50 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Chicago Bears are planning to start quarterback Caleb Williams on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons, according to multiple reports. Williams missed three games due to a torn hamstring and this week was able to return to practice at full capacity and took the starter's reps. He is officially listed as questionable for their Week 6 game, but a full week of practice showed he was trending in the right direction.Before going down with his injury, Williams played in two games: a 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers and a 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings, the game where he suffered the torn hamstring. He had a 65.6 completion percentage, 407 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in his two appearances.Williams reposted a compilation video on TikTok earlier on Saturday that had many believing he was celebrating his return. The video starts with a compilation of criticisms of how he reacted to his injury, followed by a message from a fictional character from the Chicago-based show "The Bear," who says, "I think that flicked a switch in me where I was like, f--- you. Watch this." The video then goes into highlights of Williams playing. 
The 24-year-old has openly criticized how people have reacted to his injury. When he was carted off, Williams gave a thumbs-up and raised his fist, which, to many, made it seem like the injury was very severe. Shortly after, there were reports that Williams may not miss a game.Williams feels his "character has been attacked" and said to the media this week, "It was a hamstring tear and a pretty serious one. We got a grade, but I wouldn't say it's deserved to be put out there after all the false ones. So next question."In his absence, the Bears have leaned on Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum, who were able to record two wins of the three games without their starter. Chicago is coming off a 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers. 
In Week 5's loss, head coach Ben Johnson benched Bagent for Keenum after Bagent went 12-of-21 with 87 yards, two picks and no touchdowns. Keenum didn't fare much better, going 11-of-19 with 108 yards, one interception and no touchdowns. Getting Williams back should be a big boost for the Bears offense, as they sit at 3-2 in a difficult division where the race is close and the top team, the Vikings, have yet to lose. Williams was drafted as the top pick in the 2024 draft and helped lead the team to the playoffs in his second season with the team. He did not miss a game in his first two seasons.

title: Collin Simmons injury: Texas star EDGE helped off field, leaves game vs. Florida - CBS Sports
description: The nation's leading sack artist was helped off the field
body:

    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:55 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        Locked in a dog fight with Florida early in the fourth quarter, No. 7 Texas saw its star pass rusher Colin Simmons go down with an apparent leg injury. Simmons was tended to on the field by the medical staff before being helped off of the field and into the medical tent while putting minimal weight on his right leg. Simmons was later shown leaving the tent and getting on a cart to be taken to the back for further evaluations. Simmons came into Week 7 as the nation's leader in sacks with 9.5 and added another against Florida to reach 10.5 just six games into the season. Simmons entered the year as a projected first-round draft pick and has put himself in the conversation to go No. 1 overall with his play through this season. 
He's on the short list alongside Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith for the title of the best player in college football, and Longhorns fans will hold their breath waiting for an official update on his status going forward. Losing Simmons for any extended period of time would be a significant blow to the Texas defense that has been among the best in college football. Simmons leads the team in sacks by a wide margin, with Maraad Watson coming into the game second on the team with 3.0 sacks this season. 
Simmons' ability to pressure the quarterback is crucial to their defense, allowing the Longhorns to be more aggressive on the outside, knowing quarterbacks will rarely have the opportunity to sit back and push the ball downfield.

After a sluggish start, UNLV has looked the part of one of the Group of 6's top teams as the season's worn on, and Dan Mullen's crew still has the dream of a conference title and possible Playoff berth in their sights. To get there, they'll need to run the tables and after passing a stiff test in Week 6, they get another in the form of a Falcons team that's been rolling.
